The test image shows a **stem** at a branch junction with:
- Dark blackish/grayish discoloration at the node
- Dense grayish-dusty/powdery covering over the stem tissue
- Orange-tan streaking on the stem underneath
- Cracking/deteriorating stem tissue
- White areas visible within the darker lesion

This points strongly to **Gray_Mold** (Botrytis) with its characteristic dense gray-brown spore mass on stems, or possibly **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**. Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The Gray Mold stem reference shows a tan-brown lesion on a green stem — this doesn't match the test image well. The test image shows a **very dark (nearly black) stem lesion** at a branch junction with a grayish dusty/velvety covering and orange-tan internal streaking.

Key analysis:
- **Test image**: dark-black stem at node, grayish powdery/velvety covering, white patches within the dark mass, orange-tan streaking on the underlying stem tissue
- **Gray Mold reference**: tan-brown lesion on green stem — much lighter, different character
- The very dark "almost black" coloration with grayish sporulation matches **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers** description: "large, irregularly shaped, dark-brown to almost black cankers" with "Vascular and pith tissue directly above and below cankers develop brown streaks and become cracked and dry"
- The grayish dusty appearance is consistent with Alternaria conidia (spores in chains, olive-brown to dark brown)
- The orange-tan streaking underneath matches the described internal vascular browning
